newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sri Lanka plans to issue end-Oct diesel, jet tender.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka plans to issue end-Oct diesel, jet tender.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) plans to issue a tender to buy a combined cargo of diesel and jet fuel for end-October delivery, a CPC source said on Monday.
"We would issue the tender either tomorrow or the day after," he said. "It will be for end-October delivery."

He said the tender would seek 20,000 tonnes, or 150,000 barrels, of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel and 5,000-6,000 tonnes, 37,500-45,000 barrels, of aviation jet fuel, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Colombo.
The tender might close on October 2, he said.

The source said the return of rainfall has restored hydropower back to normal capacity and this has allowed CPC to resume importing its usual two combined cargoes or about 300,000 barrels of middle-distillates a month.

In its last tender, CPC bought 160,000 barrels of diesel and 40,000 barrels of jet fuel from Swiss trader Glencore at 89 cents a barrel above Singapore spot quotes for October 11-12 delivery, c-and-f Colombo.
During the peak of the dry season in June, CPC bought 470,000 barrels of diesel.
